analysis.title: Introduction to Undirected and Directed Graphs
analysis.diagram:
The blackboard shows two graph diagrams:
1. On the left: An undirected graph with three vertices labeled 'a', 'b', and 'c' forming a triangle where all nodes are connected to each other.
2. On the right: A directed graph with the same three vertices. There is a directed arrow pointing from 'b' to 'a', another pointing from 'a' to 'c', and two parallel arrows in opposite directions between 'b' and 'c' (one pointing from 'b' to 'c', and one from 'c' to 'b').
analysis.explanation: This lecture visualizes the fundamental difference between undirected and directed graphs. In undirected graphs, edges represent bidirectional, symmetric relationships. In directed graphs, edges (also called arcs) have a specific direction representing one-way relationships, which allows for asymmetric connections and multiple distinct paths between the same pair of nodes (as seen between 'b' and 'c').
important_points: An undirected graph has edges with no orientation (e.g., connection between 'a' and 'b' is mutual).
A directed graph features edges with orientation, indicated by arrows.
A directed graph can have separate, directional paths going both ways between two nodes.
